groupRevisionArguments.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
EDIT TARGET = image 1, the already cyberpunk-enhanced FIVE-person group photograph. Image 2 is the revised Dries avatar, a HEADGEAR DESIGN REFERENCE ONLY for the very tall man at the extreme left. Image 3 is the original real photograph, the absolute identity, face, smile, body-proportion and room reference for all five people.
Make the requested NEXT VERSION: everybody gets visibly MORE cybernetic equipment, while preserving all five actual faces, friendly smiles, real hair, glasses, original left-to-right order, very tall Dries at left, relative heights and builds, camera view, group spacing and the recognizable MIT room. Keep a PHOTOGRAPHIC finish; do not turn the group into cartoons.

EXTREME LEFT / DRIES: replace the face-obscuring square green eyepatch with the inventive OPEN-FACED HELMET design from image 2: skeletal titanium/graphite head shell, translucent emerald processor-fin crest, cyan curved fiberoptic ribs, intricate ear modules and backward sensor prongs. Both eyes, eyebrows, nose, cheeks and entire smile clearly VISIBLE. Green HUD is a very small transparent side display at the temple, outside the eye, not an eyepatch. Preserve his actual photographed face/hair, not the illustrated avatar's face. Add denser integrated backpack circuitry, shoulder tool modules, fiber-optic chest routes and mechanical arm/leg braces, still showing the green sweatshirt and tan trousers.
SECOND FROM LEFT, glasses/dark hair: keep face/glasses fully visible. Upgrade the puzzle-master suit with nested articulated collar and shoulder assemblies, intricate iridescent violet neural side modules above/behind the ears, forearm gauntlets with fine light traces, a layered translucent geometric puzzle console floating above one wrist and small non-weapon sensor devices hovering beside shoulder. Most advanced gear.
CENTER, light hair/glasses: keep face/glasses visible. Elaborate silver/gold/cyan puzzle-master crown and open-face neural ring, layered high-tech mantle, intricate chest processor modules, sophisticated glowing circuit forearms and nested 3D holographic puzzle-lattice above palm. He and the second man are the TWO most technologically advanced figures. Their equipment looks a generation ahead, beautiful and mysterious, not sinister.
SECOND FROM RIGHT / SON: substantially more visible black/cobalt cyber-engineer gear: open-faced GPU neural headband behind his real glasses, compact processor modules around the back of the head, elegant angular shoulder exoskeletons, fiberoptic jacket panels, articulated forearm and finger overlays and slim leg braces. Keep his actual smiling face fully visible and his blazer/check shirt recognizable.
EXTREME RIGHT / MATT: more intricate charcoal/amber/cyan cyber suit, open-faced angular neural headgear around temples and back of crown, sophisticated layered shoulder/collar equipment, detailed chest circuits and compact sensor array, articulated forearm and thigh/shin exoskeletons. His actual smile, eyes, hair and body remain recognizable.

Give all five distinctly visible head, torso and limb upgrades. Add realistic tiny hardware details, bolts, circuit nodes, cables, luminous inlays and physically attached equipment, but no overwhelming bulk. No face masks or dark visors. Keep every face clear and near-identical to the original photograph. Original hands stay anatomically correct; avoid changing their poses further.
BACKGROUND: preserve the room, ceiling beams, daylight windows, tables, red chairs and background attendees. Increase the future-lab enhancement moderately: integrated luminous circuit channels in the ceiling, a few floating translucent abstract colored puzzle grids, practical glowing bench modules. Natural warm daylight plus blue-green/amber accent light. No darkness or smoky nightclub, no logos or new readable text.
No added foreground people, duplicates, animals, weapons, battle props, labels, headlines, names, scores or watermarks. Cybernetics are playful editorial fantasy. Keep the same landscape 4:3 composition and realistic group-photo identity.

editorFollowup: Lighthearted first-person dispatch about meeting Tufa, the unnamed puzzle masters and Matt, head of testing; then a more inventive open-faced Dries helmet and more cybernetic gear on every person in the group photo. Revised previews must be shown before publication.

avatarRevisionArguments.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
EDIT the existing full-body Dries cyber-engineer avatar (image 1). Image 2 is the original real photograph; the EXTREME LEFT very tall man is the only real likeness reference. Preserve the improved recognizable face, friendly smile, real swept brown hair, very tall lean long-limbed physique, full-body pose, hands holding GPU, detailed dark exosuit, green/cyan tubes, backpack and cream background. Make ONE requested design revision: replace the ordinary headset and bulky eye-covering green monocle with a much more CREATIVE OPEN-FACED HELMET.
Design a sophisticated asymmetric skeletal neural helmet: beautifully articulated titanium/graphite structure wrapping the back and sides of his head, an elevated split crest made of small translucent emerald processor fins and elegant cyan fiber-optic arches, mechanical hinges above the ears, finely engineered antenna/sensor prongs angled BACKWARD. This must read as an inventive bespoke cybernetic helmet, not just headphones and not a crown.
Keep the FRONT completely OPEN so BOTH REAL EYES, brows, nose, cheeks, jaw and entire smiling mouth are visibly uncovered. Show his brown hair/fringe through the open crest. REMOVE the opaque rectangular grid eyepatch. Replace it with a tiny transparent green HUD lens projected BESIDE his right temple, outside the contour of the eye and cheek, so neither eye is obscured. Preserve the green identity accent in the side sensor and helmet fins.
Keep the existing polished painterly 3D comic style, warm light, cream background, one person only, head and feet fully inside the frame with a little margin above the new helmet. No extra characters, text, names, logos, card frame, watermark, weapons, face mask, face visor or facial implants. Identity, body, pose and outfit remain consistent; revise only the headgear as requested.

groupArguments.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: editorial cyberpunk photo edit for The ARC Daily Digest, submitted for human approval.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the original real group photograph at an ARC event at MIT. Image 2 is ONLY a costume continuity reference for the tall man on the extreme left; it is not an extra person and its illustrated face must NOT replace the photographed face.

Create a lightly but unmistakably cybernetically enhanced PHOTOGRAPH of this exact scene. Preserve the original 4:3 landscape composition, all FIVE foreground people, the exact left-to-right order, poses, hands, body builds, relative heights, faces, recognizable hairstyles, glasses, genuine smiles and friendly candid mood. The man at the extreme left is particularly tall; preserve his tall long-limbed proportions. Keep all five actual faces visibly identifiable, unobscured eyes where possible, natural skin texture, no beautification or invented facial features.

Costumes, left to right:
1. Very tall man in pale green sweatshirt: tasteful graphite exosuit panels over his clothing, cyan and green piping, a compact green-grid monocle over his RIGHT eye and a modest GPU backpack inspired by reference 2. His actual brown hair, face and smile come from the photo.
2. Dark-haired man with rectangular glasses and striped polo: one of the TWO mysterious ARC3 puzzle masters. Give him sophisticated, beautiful, highly advanced graphite/iridescent cybernetic equipment, fine blue-violet circuitry, neural ear/temple interfaces, articulated shoulder hardware, translucent floating geometric puzzle-grid interfaces near his shoulder and wrist, no readable symbols. Keep his glasses and entire smiling face.
3. Fair-haired man with glasses and grey cardigan: the OTHER puzzle master. Equally more high-tech than everyone else, complementary elegant dark-silver tech mantle and layered neural crown that leaves his hair/face visible, delicate cyan-gold circuitry and subtle hovering geometric grid instruments. Both middle puzzle masters have noticeably the most advanced gear, clever and enigmatic, friendly not sinister.
4. Second from right, smiling East Asian man with black rectangular glasses and dark blazer: black cyber-engineer jacket, small dense GPU modules on shoulders, blue illuminated temple frame integrated with his own glasses, and subtle wrist interface. Preserve his real face and smile.
5. Extreme right, tall dark-haired man in black shirt: refined charcoal cyberpunk jacket with slim metallic collar, amber/cyan tech seams, compact earpiece and forearm module. Preserve his face, relaxed posture and smile.

Background: retain the real MIT indoor event room, perspective, exposed ceiling beams, windows, tables, red chairs and background attendees. Tastefully augment the beams with cyan light channels, add a few transparent abstract ARC-like colored puzzle grids and restrained future-lab details. Preserve the daylight and warm room light; cinematic teal accents without turning the whole photo dark or neon. Tech should look physically present and integrated with realistic shadows/reflections. Editorial fantasy costume, not a claim about real hardware.
Do not add, remove, duplicate or reposition foreground people. No helmets hiding faces, no masks, no weapons, no combat armor, no huge robots, no animals. Do not invent badge text. No headline, captions, names, scores, readable new words, logos or watermark. Keep the original scene recognizable as a group photo with tasteful cybernetic upgrades.

avatarArguments.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / stylized-concept.
Asset type: updated reusable full-body Dries Smit cyber-engineer avatar for The ARC Daily Digest; human review candidate.
Image 1 is the identity and real body-proportion reference: ONLY the VERY TALL man on the EXTREME LEFT of the supplied group photo. The user explicitly identifies that man as Dries Smit and asks to improve his existing avatar based on his actual appearance. Do not depict any of the other four people.
Image 2 is the established avatar COSTUME AND ART STYLE reference. Make a new sibling version of this character: keep the dark graphite cyber-engineer suit, small square GREEN GRID eyepiece over his RIGHT eye, cyan/green illuminated tubes, fan-cooled graphics-card backpack and unbranded graphics card in his hands, but improve his likeness and proportions from the real photograph.
Show ONE full-body person alone, head to boots entirely in frame, on a pale warm cream studio background with subtle ground shadow. He is very tall, long-legged, lean, naturally proportioned with a longer torso and limbs, NOT stocky or superhero muscular. Preserve the photographed man's real youthful clean-shaven face, soft jaw, swept brown hair with natural fringe, friendly broad natural smile, and distinctive approachable expression. Facial likeness comes from the extreme-left real man, not the generic face of the old illustration. Slight three-quarter stance, relaxed friendly engineer holding a single unbranded GPU at waist/chest height, two natural hands with correct fingers.
Polished detailed painterly 3D comic editorial rendering matching the established character. More true to the real person while retaining recognizable costume continuity. Keep headgear small enough to see his hair and most of his face. The right-eye eyepiece can cover only that one eye; show the smile clearly.
No other people, no animals, no text, no card frame, no badges, no labels, no logos, no watermark. Cybernetic hardware is a playful editorial costume.
